From the east came a small but ambitious band of Holnareem, seeking the mineral wealth of dreaded Mount Greb, which dominated the horizon like the rusted spire of a filthy crown. Their leader was the metallic giant named Koniguldon.

Preferring peaceful trade, they tried to avoid ruthless slaughter whenever possible. Unfortunately, sometimes this wasn't possible.

As they came near to Mount Greb, which was surrounded by vast marshlands (impassable to their kind, as their immense weight would simply cause them to sink in the mud), they found a tiny squallid village of men situated in front of the only accessible path to their destination. This speck of poverty and indolence was called Chesha.

When Koniguldon demanded to speak to their chief, he was informed that they didn't have one. Incredulous, he asked who made decisions for the village.

A wild-haired, hunched-over woman covered in crude paints told him there was no government, and that behavior was determined by custom alone. Anyone who deviated from custom was instantly killed. Furthermore, there was absolutely no custom permitting them to allow giant men made of animate metal to either enter or pass through their village.

Koniguldon presented them with wonderous works of crafted art, tools for making their menial tasks easier, etc. His offers only seemed to anger the villagers. His next tactic was to ask for another way of accessing the path to Mount Gelb. They insisted there was no other way.

The villagers quickly realized that the Holnareem had no intention of turning back, and they began to scream and tear their own flesh. Soon a carpet of living bodies barred the way through Chesha. Exasperated, Koniguldon recused himself from further negotiations, and appointed his most trusted lieutenant, a fair young Holnareem named Jamus. But his attempts at persuation were no more effective.

Shortly before the next dawn, the surrounding marshlands were filled with wild screams and the crunching sounds of breaking bones. The massive feet of the Holnareem left deep, bloody footprints as they marched down the narrow, winding path toward Mount Greb.
